title: Reasons & Contrast: から, ので, が, けれども
description: Giving reasons with から and ので (and how each attaches), saying 'but' with が and けれども/けど.

points.title: から (1): because, since
points.summary: Clause + から = 'because …'. The reason comes first. It attaches to plain or polite forms; nouns and な-adjectives take だ.
points.body:
**[reason]から、[result]**: the reason always comes **before** から.

It attaches to plain or polite forms:
- Verb: 雨が降っている**から** / 降っています**から**
- い-adjective: 暑い**から**
- Noun / な-adjective: 学生**だから**, 静か**だから** (don't drop だ!)

から can end a sentence when answering 'why?': どうして来なかったの？—忙しかった**から**。

から sounds more **subjective and direct** (my reason). It's natural with requests, opinions and invitations: 暑いから、窓を開けてください.

Don't confuse it with **noun + から = from** (東京から) and **て-form + から = after** (食べてから).
examples: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っているから、{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{行|い}きます。
It's raining, so I'll take an umbrella.
{明日|あした}は{休|やす}みだから、{遅|おそ}くまで{寝|ね}ます。
Tomorrow's a day off, so I'll sleep in.
どうして{食|た}べないの？—おなかがいっぱいだから。
Why aren't you eating? — Because I'm full.

points.title: ので: because (softer, more objective)
points.summary: Clause + ので = 'because / so'. Softer and more polite than から. Nouns and な-adjectives take な: 学生なので.
points.body:
**ので** also gives a reason, but it presents it as a **natural, objective cause**, so it sounds softer and more polite. It's the usual choice for excuses and explanations to superiors: 頭が痛い**ので**、早く帰ってもいいですか.

**How it attaches (the big difference from から):**
- Verb / い-adjective: plain form, as with から: 降る**ので**, 高い**ので**.
- Noun / な-adjective: **な** instead of だ: 学生**なので**, 静か**なので**. 学生だので is wrong.

In casual speech it often becomes **んで**: 忙しいんで.

Unlike から, ので normally **doesn't end a sentence** as a bare answer to 'why?'.
examples: {明日|あした}は{試験|しけん}があるので、{今日|きょう}は{早|はや}く{寝|ね}ます。
I have an exam tomorrow, so I'll go to bed early tonight.
この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}かなので、よく{眠|ねむ}れます。
This room is quiet, so I can sleep well.
{子供|こども}なので、まだ{一人|ひとり}で{行|い}けません。
They're a child, so they can't go alone yet.

points.title: が (2): but, however
points.summary: Clause + が, clause = 'but'. Also used to soften an opening (すみませんが…).
points.body:
After a **complete clause** (usually polite), が means 'but':
- 日本語は難しいです**が**、面白いです。

It's slightly formal and very common in polite speech and writing. Casual equivalents: けど / けれど / けれども.

It's also used as a **softener** that introduces a request or question without real contrast:
- すみません**が**、駅はどこですか。
- 失礼です**が**、お名前は？

How to tell it apart from **subject が**: subject が follows a **noun** (雨**が**降る). 'But' が follows a full clause ending in a verb, adjective or です (降ります**が**).
examples: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいですが、{面白|おもしろ}いです。
Japanese is difficult, but it's interesting.
すみませんが、ちょっと{手伝|てつだ}ってください。
Sorry, but could you help me a bit?
{高|たか}かったですが、{買|か}いました。
It was expensive, but I bought it.

points.title: けれども / けれど / けど: but, although
points.summary: Clause + けれども = 'but / although'. From most formal to most casual: けれども → けれど → けど.
points.body:
**けれども** means the same as 'but' が. Its shorter forms are progressively more casual:
- **けれども**: polite or written
- **けれど**: neutral
- **けど**: everyday conversation

It attaches to plain or polite forms: 高い**けど**, 高いです**けれども**, 学生**だけど** (keep だ with nouns and な-adjectives).

Like が, it can **soften** a statement or trail off politely, leaving the conclusion unsaid: ちょっと用事があるんですけど… (I have something to do, so… i.e. I can't).

Unlike のに ('even though', N4), けれども can be followed by any kind of clause, including requests and intentions.
examples: {天気|てんき}はいいけれども、{寒|さむ}いです。
The weather is nice, but it's cold.
{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだけど、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い。
I took medicine, but my head still hurts.
{行|い}きたいんですけど、{時間|じかん}がなくて…
I'd like to go, but I don't have time…

questions.prompt: {暑|あつ}い（　）、{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けてください。
questions.explanation: い-adjective + **から** directly (no だ): 暑いから.
notes: のから isn't a form.
な belongs with ので (静かなので), never with から.
い-adjectives attach directly to から. だ is only for nouns and な-adjectives (静かだから).
questions.translation: It's hot, so please open the window.

questions.prompt: A：どうして{食|た}べないの？　B：おなかがいっぱいだ（　）。
questions.explanation: Answering 'why?' with a bare reason uses **から**, and it follows だ.
notes: ので doesn't attach to だ. It would be いっぱいなので, and even then a bare ので answer sounds unfinished.
のから isn't a form.
Since だ is already there, だなので would double the copula.
questions.translation: A: Why aren't you eating? B: Because I'm full.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}み（　）、{遅|おそ}くまで{寝|ね}ます。
questions.explanation: A noun before から needs **だ**: 休みだから. (休みから would mean 'from the holiday'.)
notes: のから isn't a form.
休みから means 'from the day off', not 'because'.
な is for ので (休みなので), not から.
questions.translation: Tomorrow's a day off, so I'll sleep late.

questions.prompt: この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}か（　）ので、よく{眠|ねむ}れます。
questions.explanation: な-adjectives and nouns take **な** before ので: 静かなので.
notes: 静かのので isn't a form.
だので is wrong. だ is used before から (静かだから), not ので.
静かでので isn't a form.
questions.translation: This room is quiet, so I sleep well.

questions.prompt: （To your boss）すみません、{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}い（　）、{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}ってもいいですか。
questions.explanation: **ので** gives the reason softly and politely, which is ideal when asking a superior for permission.
notes: だので is never correct.
い-adjectives attach to ので directly. なので is only for nouns and な-adjectives.
のに means 'even though'. 'My head hurts, even though…' makes no sense and can't be followed by a request.
questions.translation: Excuse me, I have a headache, so may I go home early?

questions.prompt: {弟|おとうと}はまだ{子供|こども}（　）、{一人|ひとり}で{行|い}けません。
notes: のので isn't a form.
だので is a common mistake. ので needs な after nouns.
子供ので is missing な.
questions.translation: My little brother is still a child, so he can't go alone.

questions.prompt: {日本語|にほんご}は{難|むずか}しいです（　）、{面白|おもしろ}いです。
notes: ので has the same problem as から.
から ('because') would mean 'it's interesting because it's difficult', which isn't the intended contrast.
と after です doesn't connect clauses like this.

questions.prompt: すみません（　）、{駅|えき}はどこですか。
questions.explanation: **が** softens an opening before a question, with no real contrast.
notes: すみませんと isn't used to introduce a question.
すみませんので has the same problem.
すみませんから would mean 'because I'm sorry', which is illogical.
questions.translation: Excuse me, where is the station?

questions.prompt: {高|たか}かったです（　）、{買|か}いました。
notes: まで can't follow です.
ので would mean you bought it because it was expensive, which is odd.
から has the same problem as ので.
questions.translation: It was expensive, but I bought it.

questions.prompt: {天気|てんき}は（　）けれども、{寒|さむ}いです。
questions.explanation: い-adjective (plain) + **けれども** directly: いいけれども.
notes: な is only used before nouns, and いい isn't a な-adjective.
よく is the adverb form, which can't end a clause before けれども.
い-adjectives attach to けれども directly. だ is only for nouns and な-adjectives.
questions.translation: The weather is nice, but it's cold.

questions.prompt: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだ（　）、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
questions.explanation: Took medicine, but it still hurts: **けれども**.
notes: ので has the same problem.
飲んだまで isn't a natural form here.
から would make the medicine the cause of the headache.
questions.translation: I took medicine, but my head still hurts.

questions.prompt: Which is the **most casual** way to say 'but' in conversation?
questions.explanation: Register from formal to casual: けれども → けれど → **けど**. 'But' が is fairly formal.
notes: けれども is the most formal of the family.
が ('but') is polite/formal, typical after です/ます.
けれど is neutral, between けれども and けど.

questions.prompt: ここは{静|しず}か（　）から、ここで{勉強|べんきょう}しましょう。
notes: な goes with ので (静かなので), not から.
のから isn't a form.
でから isn't a form.
questions.translation: It's quiet here, so let's study here.

questions.prompt: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っている（　）、{試合|しあい}は{中止|ちゅうし}になりました。
notes: Verbs attach to ので directly — なので is only for nouns/な-adjectives.
だので is never correct.
のに ('even though') is illogical: the rain is the reason.
questions.translation: Because it's raining, the match was cancelled.

questions.prompt: {漢字|かんじ}は{難|むずか}しい（　）、{面白|おもしろ}いです。
notes: い-adjectives never take だ — 難しいだが is wrong.
なが isn't a form.
難しいのが would make 'being difficult' a noun subject.

questions.prompt: {学生|がくせい}（　）けど、お{金|かね}がありません。
questions.explanation: Noun + **だ** + けど (casual) — or です + けど (polite).
notes: のけど isn't a form.
な before けど is wrong (it's for ので / のに).
でけど isn't a form.
questions.translation: I'm a student, but I don't have any money.
